**Phase 2 post-training contributes the larger gain.** Compared with a freshly trained Phase-1 model, it improves offline ranking metrics (MRR) by roughly **35–50%** (p. 7).

Details from the paper:

- **Phase 2:** The 35–50% gain is measured on the Phase-1 training cutoff date, when the Phase-1 model is at its freshest. The benefit grows over time, reaching roughly **80% after two weeks**. The authors say this reflects both task-specific adaptation and the growing staleness of the less frequently updated Phase-1 backbone (p. 7).
- **Phase 1:** Using the Phase-1 foundational LLM as the base model improves offline ranking metrics by about **10–20%** compared with an off-the-shelf (OSS) LLM backbone (p. 7, Table 1).

The two gains are measured against different baselines. Phase 1 is compared with an OSS model, while Phase 2 is compared with a freshly trained Phase-1 model. Still, Phase 2's reported relative gain is clearly the larger of the two (p. 7, Table 1).
